subject: Observability overage smoothing & annual commit credits
messages:
From: Alicia Gomez <procurement@brightshore.io>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jul 2025 09:13:00 -0700
Subject: Observability overage smoothing & annual commit credits

Hi Markus,

Quick note from procurement at BrightShore — we ran the Q2 usage report and saw a ~60% spike in tracing/retention consumption tied to a short customer investigation in June. We're comfortable with the underlying usage growth, but the overage this month makes our CFO nervous.

Two asks:
- Can Redwood offer a temporary smoothing (monthly cap / blended overage) so the spike doesn't blow our variability budget?
- For our annual renewal conversation, what does a committed-observability-credit structure look like? We want a path that moves us to a predictable monthly spend while preserving coverage for burst tracing/retention.

Attached the Q3 invoice and our internal usage extract for context.

Thanks — can you loop in pricing and the product owner?

— Alicia Gomez
Procurement, BrightShore Health
[Attachment: Q3-invoice.pdf (PDF)]

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Gomez <procurement@brightshore.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jul 2025 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Observability overage smoothing & annual commit credits

Hi Alicia — thanks for the context and the files. Looping in Ben (pricing lead) and Soojin (product for observability) to propose options.

High level — we can do two things quickly:
1) Smoothing pilot: temporary blended overage cap for the next 2 billing cycles (can be applied retroactively to July usage) to reduce immediate variance.
2) Annual commit + burst buffer: a committed token/GB pool for retention + a smaller burst reserve priced at a reduced overage rate.

Ben / Soojin — can you take a look at the attached invoice and Alicia's usage extract and propose a short (two-email) path that gets them to a pilot smoothing now and a draft credit schedule for their renewal? Alicia, we'll try to keep the ask to you minimal — a DocuSign for the pilot plus typical SOW language if you want the buffer codified.

-Markus

--
Markus Klein
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Alicia Gomez <procurement@brightshore.io>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jul 2025 11:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Observability credit options (pilot + annual structure)

Alicia / Markus — attached is a first-pass credit schedule and a short counteroffer for smoothing. Summary here:

Option A — 2-month smoothing pilot (recommended)
- Apply a blended overage cap equal to 120% of May baseline for July & August.
- Retroactive adjustment available for July only (one-time).
- No change to product quotas; invoicing note + credit applied to next invoice.
- Minimal admin: sign the one-page pilot addendum (DocuSign).

Option B — Annual committed credits + burst buffer
- Commit to an annual observability credit pool (GB-days + trace-seconds): 20% discount to list on committed portion.
- Burst reserve at 50% of committed price for additional usage up to 2x monthly baseline.
- Rolling true-up every quarter; unused committed credits can be carried for one quarter.

We attached: observability_credit_schedule_v1.pdf (line-by-line pricing), a sample one-page pilot addendum, and the SOW draft (sow-observability-draft.docx).

Questions for BrightShore:
- What monthly baseline would you want us to anchor the pilot to (May/June average)?
- Any mandatory internal signatories we should include on the DocuSign?

If this looks good, Markus / I can prepare a DocuSign for the pilot and a commitment schedule for your renewal team.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
[Attachment: observability_credit_schedule_v1.pdf (PDF)]

From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@brightshore.io>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Alicia Gomez <procurement@brightshore.io>
Date: Thu, 24 Jul 2025 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Observability overage smoothing & annual commit credits

Ben / Markus — thanks for the quick turnaround and the materials. We ran this by our finance lead and agree to the pilot approach (Option A) with one tweak: rather than anchoring to May only, we'd like a blended baseline of April–June average to avoid month-to-month variance.

Two items before DocuSign:
- Confirm we can cap retroactive adjustment to the July invoice only (no retroactive credits beyond July).
- Confirm the pilot addendum includes an explicit rollback clause if our usage normalizes below baseline after August.

If you can confirm those two points, we'll get signatures on the pilot addendum this week and then work with you on the annual commit sizing conversation.

Thanks — copying Alicia for sign-off.

— Daniel Park
Head of Cloud Ops, BrightShore Health
[Attachment: none]
